About Formlabs:
A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.
Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.
That’s what we do.
At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

As a Manufacturing Engineer II on the Ohio engineering team, reporting to the Head of Continuous Improvement & Engineering, you'll be the person who connects our production lines to software. You'll build the tools operators use every shift, link our equipment to our data, and design the fixtures and changes that make lines faster and more reliable. Your work will raise yield and uptime, help scale existing production, and get new equipment to rate.

Design, build, and maintain factory software: operator GUIs, line-side tools, data collection, and traceability for filling, labeling, marking, and packaging.
Connect production equipment (PLCs, printers, scanners, cameras, RFID readers) to our databases, ERP, and MES.
Use AI coding tools to deliver quickly, while owning code quality through version control, testing, code review, and documentation.
Design fixtures, brackets, guards, and change parts in CAD, and release drawings to machine shops and vendors.
Work across hardware, production, quality, and engineering teams to turn line problems into solutions that hold up in production.
Lead continuous improvement projects on existing lines, using production data to raise yield and uptime and cut scrap and changeover time.
Build up production readiness for new equipment and processes: write requirements, specify equipment and integrators, and support FAT, SAT, commissioning, and getting to rate.
Write and maintain clear work instructions and SOPs, and train operators and maintenance technicians on new tools and processes.
Spend real time on the production floor troubleshooting with production and maintenance, and drive root cause and corrective action.
Build SQL queries and dashboards that make line performance visible to the team.
Follow and improve safe work practices in a chemical manufacturing environment.
You:
Have a BS in Mechanical, Electrical, or Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related engineering field.
1+ year of industry experience in manufacturing, automation, or hardware; relevant internships and co-ops count.
Strong proficiency in Python and working knowledge of C/C++.
Fluent, daily user of AI coding assistants, with the judgment to review, test, and correct what they produce.
Have built graphical user interfaces that real users depend on (for example Qt/PyQt, a web front end, or an HMI).
Experience with SQL and relational databases, and an understanding of how ERP and MES systems fit together on a plant floor.
Proficient in 3D CAD (SolidWorks, Onshape, or similar) and able to create and read engineering drawings, including basic GD&T.
Fluent in written and spoken English, and able to write clear, step-by-step work instructions.
Are hands-on and want to be on the floor: comfortable in PPE, around chemicals and moving equipment, and willing to get your hands dirty.
Independent self-starter with a strong bias for action and a real sense of ownership who finishes what you start.
Willingness and ability to travel approximately 10–20% of the time.
Bonus Skills
3+ years of industry experience in manufacturing, automation, or hardware.
Experience with PLCs and HMIs (Allen-Bradley Studio 5000, Siemens TIA Portal, or similar) and industrial protocols such as EtherNet/IP, Modbus, OPC UA, or MQTT.
